newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bank Pekao mulls PZU insurer stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Polish bank Pekao mulls PZU insurer stake - paper.

text.p: The head of Poland's largest insurer, state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU) said state-owned bank Pekao SA was mulling taking a stake in PZU and pulling out of another insurer Amplico Life.

"Pekao SA, which is one of the serious candidates for our shareholders has taken serious steps to withdraw from Amplico. They have announced they were ready to sell their stake," Jan Monkiewicz told Gazeta Wyborcza in an interview.
"Pekao SA is seriously thinking of acquiring some of our shares," he added.
Pekao has a 45 percent stake in Amplico Life, a joint-venture with U.S. American Insurance Group (AIG) which holds the remaining 55 percent of shares.
Pekao officials declined to comment on the report and Amplico Life said it would make a statement in the next few days.

Earlier this month PZU, which controls about 60 percent of the non-life insurance market in Poland, announced it would seek to raise $200-300 million through a private placement to a group of selected institutional investors.
It said none of the institutional investors would have a controlling stake in the firm.
Monkiewicz also told Wyborcza PZU planned a flotation on the Warsaw bourse in the fourth quarter of 1997 or later and considered also listing on the London Stock Exchange.
